sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
Wayne County splits the job between two functions. Tax Administration sets values. The Tax Collector bills and takes payment, at P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Both are reached from the county tax page.

That page links a billings search, rates, forms, maps, relief programs and a list of tax foreclosure sales, so you can look up a balance before you list the house.

  • Collector: balances, payoff letters, payment options
  • Administration: value, appeals, relief applications
  • Register of Deeds in Goldsboro: deeds and deeds of trust

Downloadable appraisal data and the schedule of values for the 2025 reappraisal are posted there too. A buyer or investor comparing several parcels can use them, and you can see how the county priced land and buildings.

sections.h2: Wayne County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Goldsboro anchors a county of 122,278 people over 553.92 square miles. There are 55,106 housing units and 47,507 households, and owners hold 61.5% of occupied homes. Median rent is $965 a month, and about four homes in ten are rented, so many sellers here are landlords.

The county has grown slowly. It counted 122,623 people in 2010 and 117,333 in 2020, and the latest estimate sits 4.2% above 2020. New building has been modest, with 954 permits for 2025. Most owners (86.1%) stayed at the same address over the prior year, so many have not sold in years and their last real price check may be the revaluation notice itself.

The county revalued every parcel as of 2025 and mailed notices in March. Its revaluation page describes a base of more than 64,000 parcels. Revaluation changes assessed value only. The commissioners and city or town boards set rates later, in budget season.

Appraisers compared recent sales, priced the cost to rebuild, and used an income method on commercial parcels. The county did not apply a flat percentage. Its example is two matching 2019 houses that ended up worth different amounts by 2025.

Wayne is above the 75,000 population line in G.S. 105-286, so the state can require an earlier reappraisal if the sales ratio drifts outside .85 to 1.15.

A reappraisal looks at local sales, so a neighborhood with new construction and steady buyers can move differently from a farm district. Compare your notice with recent sales near you before deciding whether to appeal.

Begin with the form attached to your notice. An appraiser reviews it once it reaches the Tax Office, which must happen inside 30 days of the notice date.

If the answer comes back unchanged, a second notice explains the formal hearing before the county's Board of Equalization and Review. After that comes the state Property Tax Commission. Keep copies of everything you submit, because that file is the starting point for the board hearing.

  • Strong evidence: an appraisal, written repair bids, dated damage photos, nearby sales
  • Weak grounds: what you can afford to pay, or a value near market

Outside revaluation years, use the county's non reappraisal year appeals page instead.

Statewide tax calendar as it applies to a Wayne County parcel
EventTiming
Listing windowFirst business day of January to January 31
Bill dueSeptember 1
Interest beginsJanuary 6, at 2%
Hearing board startsBetween first Monday of April and first Monday of May
State appeal30 days from the board's mailed decision

After February 1, interest runs at three-quarters of one percent monthly. Counties may adopt early payment discounts, so ask the Tax Collector what applies.

Three state programs can lower or defer a bill. Each is filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor. The Department of Revenue's 2026 form prints a $38,800 income limit, and $58,200 for the upper circuit breaker band.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000, no income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: 4% or 5% of income as a ceiling, with deferral of the rest (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Apply during listing season. The assessor must accept filings until June 1 before the tax year. Deferred amounts become a lien and come due when you sell.

The tax lien dates from January 1 of the tax year (G.S. 105-355), and a buyer takes the house with it. That is why the title company pays the balance out of your proceeds.

An unpaid lien can end in a court action and courthouse sale (G.S. 105-374), but you can redeem by paying everything owed until the sale is confirmed. The county posts its own tax foreclosure sales page.

Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff, and tell the closing office about any deferral or pending appeal so neither surprises the buyer.

sections.h2: What to ask before you list
sections.html:
• What is owed on the parcel today, and has this year's bill gone out?
  • Does a Goldsboro special assessment or nuisance abatement charge sit on it?
  • Is an appeal of the 2025 value still open?
  • Is a circuit breaker deferral on the account?

Contact the Tax Collector or use the billings search linked from the county tax page. For an inherited or vacant house, confirm the owner of record first, since bills follow the record owner.

1. Look up the parcel in the billings search and note the balance and the year it covers.
  2. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff that matches your closing date.
  3. Check whether a revaluation appeal or a circuit breaker deferral is attached to the account.
  4. Hand the payoff to your closing attorney or title company so it is paid from proceeds.
  5. After closing, confirm the new owner's name and mailing address reached the tax office.

A sale to a cash buyer follows the same list, but it usually skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the tax payoff is often the only item with a fixed deadline. Sorting out the account early keeps that closing date from slipping.

The bill follows the owner of record. An heir who has not recorded anything may still see the late owner on the account, so ask the Tax Collector who is listed and which address receives the mail.

A rented house and an empty one get the same bill. Add up each year's balance before you settle on a closing date.

If the owner of record has died, the deed history lives with the register of deeds, and the county's real estate search shows parcel details. A cash buyer or an attorney can use both to confirm title before a contract is signed.

  • Pull the parcel through the real estate search
  • Request the payoff in writing
  • Ask whether the new owner will need the January listing handled

faqs.q: What day does interest begin on a Wayne County bill?
faqs.a: January 6. The bill is due September 1, but interest holds off until that January date. It then runs at 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month afterward.

faqs.q: How many parcels did Wayne County revalue in 2025?
faqs.a: The county cites more than 64,000 parcels. Owners received notices in March 2025.

faqs.q: Does revaluation set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. Revaluation updates value. Elected boards set the rate during budget work, and the county tax page links a Tax Rates page.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the $45,000 veteran exclusion?
faqs.a: A qualifying disabled veteran owner and certain unmarried surviving spouses, with no age or income limit. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, after a Veterans Service Officer completes the VA part.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Wayne County tax payment?
faqs.a: Wayne County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Online payment is also linked from the county tax page.
